findings.description: gets() reads without a bound and overwrites the destination buffer.
findings.remediation: Replace gets() with fgets(buffer, sizeof(buffer), stdin) and handle the trailing newline.

findings.code: strcpy(buffer, input);  // Dangerous! No size checking
findings.description: Unbounded string copy/concatenation can write past the destination buffer when the source exceeds capacity.
findings.remediation: Use strlcpy()/strlcat() where available, or snprintf() with an explicit destination capacity.

findings.code: sprintf(buffer, "Hello %s", input);  // Dangerous if input is too long
findings.description: sprintf()/vsprintf() can produce output larger than the destination buffer.
findings.remediation: Use snprintf()/vsnprintf() with the destination size, and bound %s conversions.

findings.code: scanf("%s", buffer);  // Dangerous! No width specifier
findings.description: A %s/%[...] conversion without a field width or with a width exceeding destination capacity (including NUL) can overflow the buffer.
findings.remediation: Specify a field width of at most sizeof(buffer) - 1 (e.g. %63s for a 64-byte buffer), or read with fgets().

findings.code: strcat(buffer, input);  // Dangerous! No size checking
findings.description: Unbounded string copy/concatenation can write past the destination buffer when the source exceeds capacity.
findings.remediation: Use strlcpy()/strlcat() where available, or snprintf() with an explicit destination capacity.

findings.code: printf(input);  // Dangerous! User input as format string
findings.description: A non-literal format string lets an attacker control conversions such as %n and %s.
findings.remediation: Pass an explicit format: printf("%s", input) instead of printf(input).

findings.code: char *buffer = alloca(size);  // Dangerous with user-controlled size
findings.description: alloca() with a variable size can exhaust or overflow the stack.
findings.remediation: Validate the size and use a fixed bound, or allocate on the heap with malloc() and check for failure.

findings.code: memcpy(buffer, input, size);  // Dangerous if size > 100
findings.description: A raw memory operation uses a length that exceeds or is not proven to fit the destination buffer.
findings.remediation: Validate the length against the destination capacity; prefer sizeof(destination) or an explicit bounds check.
